text:
infra-alert-bot: :rotating_light: hosted-usw2 - pool-7 p95 queue latency 22.4s, active slots 60/64, small-request traffic surge (likely embeddings). dashboard: https://dash.redwood/pools/pool-7

kai: seeing a huge spike from tenant @emb-labs, traffic pattern is many short seqs. routing tried to spill to pool-9 but that one is near-cap too.

liz.m: can we temporarily increase spare slots or force a refill? autoscaler capped by reserved commits for the region.

noah: quick check command: `kubectl logs pool-7-proxy | grep enqueue | tail -n 30` -> shows enqueue latency and kvcache miss flood. pasting sample:
```
2026-03-15T21:02:11Z enqueue request id=... latency=342ms kvcache=MISS
2026-03-15T21:02:11Z enqueue request id=... latency=510ms kvcache=MISS
2026-03-15T21:02:12Z enqueue request id=... latency=1200ms kvcache=MISS
```

kai: kvcache miss rate jumped to ~78% in the last 3m, so the prefix cache eviction thrash is killing throughput for many tiny jobs. Might be the new embedding client rollout. (reaction :eyes:)

sre_oncall_mai: I’m going to trigger an emergency refill (8 nodes) and pin pool-7 to lower packing to give cushion. ETA ~4m. Also rolling back the new client if refill doesn't help.

liz.m: also enable per-tenant soft-rate-limit for emb-labs to shed ~30% of burst traffic while we stabilise. Add a short-lived override for routing policy to prefer cpu-hybrid for tiny-requests.

sre_oncall_mai: refill started (runbooks/refill -> apply). watchers: @kai @liz.m @noah.

infra-alert-bot: update: refill added 8 nodes, p95 dropped to 3.1s after ~150s, active slots 52/72. kvcache miss rate falling. Marking incident trending down. :white_check_mark:

kai: file ticket to audit embedding client rollout and add a K/V-cache warmup for tiny-req patterns.

liz.m: noted, will open a postmortem and add a dashboard panel for tiny-request qps vs kvcache miss.%

infra-alert-bot: incident closed by refill action. logs/snippets saved at https://internal.redwood/ops/incident/1769854321
